claims.statement: Zoom documents x-zm-signature as v0= followed by the hex output of an HMAC SHA-256 hash of the message v0:{x-zm-request-timestamp}:{request body} with the webhook secret token as the secret; the receiver recomputes it and compares it with the header value.

openQuestions.question: Not researched beyond existence: prefix, alphabet, length and any checksum are not stated on the pages read, and no value shape may be inferred from the examples (docs examples are placeholders or illustrative).

The two pages read describe the secret token differently: the webhooks page says Zoom hashes the body with it into x-zm-signature, while the Access page says Zoom sends the secret token in each event notification. Which wording reflects current behaviour is not settled; neither page was resolved in favour of the other.
The Access page lists a Verification Token marked deprecated (February 2025). It is a historical form that needs its own pinned source before any claim; it is not recorded as a candidate.

Established: the secret token is the HMAC key and never an input message; x-zm-signature, the v0:timestamp:body message, the plainToken challenge and the encryptedToken response are public wire values or derived outputs in the algorithm Zoom documents. Not stated: whether Zoom documents the signature or the plainToken as non-secret. This record makes no claim that they are not secrets, only that they are not the secret token.

The carrier wording conflict is recorded as claim carrier-wording-conflict and not resolved. What would settle it: a Zoom statement reconciling the pages, an archived dated snapshot showing the wording changed, or an issued event request (not permitted for this repository). No field name, header or carrier of the secret token value itself is documented, so no positive carrier can be asserted for it.

The deprecated Verification Token is a historical, era-specific credential: the Access page says both that it is deprecated and that it will be deprecated in February of 2025, and no dated archive snapshot or digest of an earlier page is held, so its era (whether it was sent in a header or body, and until when) is unresolved and it is not recorded as a family or variant.

No prefix, alphabet, length or checksum is stated for the secret token, and the signature's hex length is stated only through the algorithm (HMAC SHA-256 output in hex); examples on the pages are placeholders and no shape is inferred for the secret token.
